question: What does the Determined condition let you do?
choices: Gain an advantage on your next test
When you fail a test, add an Opportunity to it (then the condition ends)
explanation: While Determined, you can add an Opportunity to a failed test. Doing so removes the condition.
verify: when you fail a test, you can add an Opportunity

question: Which set of effects describes the Disoriented condition?
choices: Movement halved; melee attacks against you gain an advantage
No reactions; your senses count as obscured; disadvantage on Perception and similar sense-based tests
Lose two actions on your turn
Disadvantage on all tests except escaping
explanation: Disoriented means you can't use reactions, your senses always count as obscured, and Perception (and similar sensing tests) gain a disadvantage.
verify: You can’t use reactions, your senses always count as obscured

question: A Radiant becomes Empowered after swearing an Ideal. What does that grant, and when does it end?
choices: +2 to all tests until their next long rest
An advantage on all tests and Investiture refilling to max at the start of each of their turns, until the end of the scene
Immunity to damage until the end of their next turn
explanation: Empowered grants an advantage on all tests and refills Investiture to maximum at the start of each of your turns. It's removed at the end of the current scene.
verify: you gain an advantage on all tests and your Investiture refills

question: Which is true of a Prone character?
choices: Ranged attacks against them gain an advantage
They are Slowed, and melee attacks against them gain an advantage
They can't take actions until they stand
explanation: While Prone you're Slowed and melee attacks against you gain an advantage. You can Brace without cover, and after standing up your movement rate is reduced by 5 until the start of your next turn.
verify: you are Slowed and melee attacks against you gain an advantage

question: What does the Restrained condition do?
choices: Movement 0 and a disadvantage on all tests except those to escape
You can't be moved by other effects
explanation: Restrained sets your movement rate to 0 and gives a disadvantage on all tests other than escaping your bonds. (Immobilized is the one that also stops other effects moving you.)
verify: disadvantage on all tests other than those to escape your bonds

question: A character becomes Enhanced [+2 Strength]. Which of these does NOT change?
explanation: Enhanced boosts the attribute for skills, talents and things like movement, but explicitly doesn't change defenses, maximum health, maximum focus or maximum Investiture.
verify: this bonus doesn’t change your defenses, maximum health

question: How does the Exhausted condition go away?
choices: It ends at the end of the scene
After each long rest the penalty drops by 1; the condition ends at 0
A short rest removes it entirely
A DC 15 Discipline test ends it
explanation: Each long rest reduces your Exhausted penalty by 1, and the condition is removed when the penalty reaches 0. Multiple instances add together.
verify: After each long rest, reduce your Exhausted penalty by 1

question: What does the Focused condition do?
choices: Grants an advantage on Discipline tests
Reduces the focus cost of your abilities by 1
explanation: While Focused, abilities that cost focus cost 1 less.
verify: its cost is reduced by 1

question: Which of these is NOT an effect of the Surprised condition?
choices: You can't take a fast turn
Attacks against you are automatically critical hits
explanation: Surprised removes your reactions, stops you gaining a reaction at the start of combat or on your turn, bars fast turns, and costs you one action. It ends after your next turn. Nothing makes attacks auto-crit.
verify: you can’t take a fast turn

question: Can a character be Afflicted by more than one effect at the same time?
choices: Yes, but only two at once
Only if they're different damage types
explanation: Unlike most conditions, you can be Afflicted by several effects at once, resolving each separately. In combat, the damage happens at the end of each of your turns.
verify: you can be Afflicted by multiple effects simultaneously

question: When can an Unconscious PC choose to wake up?
choices: Only when healed by another character
At the end of any of their turns (no action needed), or when healed to at least 1 health
After a successful DC 15 Discipline test
explanation: A PC can choose to regain consciousness at the end of any of their turns, or when an effect heals them to at least 1 health. If they're at 0, they recover 1 health. NPCs only wake when they recover 1 health.
verify: choose to regain conscious­ ness at the end of any of your turns

question: An effect applies a condition to everything in an area that includes a cart and some crates. What happens to the objects?
choices: Objects generally ignore conditions, unless the GM decides otherwise for the story
explanation: Conditions generally only apply to characters; objects in the area ignore them, though the GM may apply a similar narrative effect when it fits.
verify: Conditions generally only apply to characters, not objects

question: Which two damage types are NOT reduced by deflect?
explanation: Deflect reduces energy, impact and keen. Spirit damage (usually from Shardblades) and vital damage (poison, suffocation, extreme cold) bypass it.
verify: This damage type is not reduced by your deflect value

question: A PC is poisoned or exposed to extreme cold. What type of damage is that by default?
explanation: Vital damage covers effects that test your constitution, such as poison, suffocation and extreme cold.
verify: poison, suffocation, and extreme cold

question: How is an injury roll calculated?
choices: d20 + armor deflect + relevant ability modifiers − 5 per existing injury
explanation: An injury roll isn't a skill test: roll a d20, add your armor's deflect and any relevant ability modifiers, and subtract 5 for each injury you already have. The result can be negative.
verify: Subtract 5 from the roll for each injury you already have

question: On the Injury Duration table, what does an injury roll result of 6 to 15 mean?
choices: Flesh wound — lasts until after a long rest
explanation: Injury roll results: 16+ flesh wound (until after a long rest); 6–15 shallow (1d6 days); 1–5 vicious (6d6 days); −5 to 0 permanent; −6 or lower death.
verify: 6 to 15 Shallow Injury

question: What injury roll result kills a character?
explanation: A result of −6 or lower is death; −5 to 0 is a permanent injury.
verify: −6 or lower Death

question: A minor NPC suffers an injury. What happens?
choices: They make an injury roll like a PC
They're immediately defeated; the PC who caused it can choose death or Unconscious
explanation: Minor NPCs are defeated as soon as they suffer an injury. The PC inflicting it can choose whether they die or fall Unconscious. Major NPCs make injury rolls like PCs.

cite.section: Ch. 9 Adventuring › Minor NPCs and Injuries

verify: If a minor NPC suffers an injury, they’re immediately defeated

question: How does recuperating during downtime affect injury healing?
choices: Each day of dedicated rest counts as two days toward healing
It heals the injury after one day
It removes one injury per week
explanation: Each downtime day spent on rest and recuperation counts as two days toward healing an injury, so you heal twice as fast.
verify: counts as two days toward healing an injury

question: When a PC suffers an injury, who decides what its effect is?
choices: The player — they can pick from or roll on the Injury Effects table, or create a custom effect with the GM
It's always a d8 roll on the table
The character who dealt the damage
explanation: The player decides the injury's effects, choosing or rolling (d8) on the Injury Effects table or working out a custom effect with the GM. The player has final say on how an injury affects their character.
verify: When your character suffers an injury, you decide its effects

question: What does a character recover after a short rest?
choices: Their recovery die result, split however they like between health and focus
explanation: A short rest (an uninterrupted hour or more) lets you roll your recovery die and add the result to health, focus or a mix of both.
verify: Add the roll result to your current health, your current focus, or a combination

question: What does a long rest provide?
choices: All lost health and focus, and the Exhausted penalty drops by 1
All health, focus and Investiture, and all injuries heal
explanation: A long rest (8+ uninterrupted hours) restores all lost health and focus and reduces your Exhausted penalty by 1.
verify: you recover all your lost health and focus

question: During a short rest, a PC chooses Tend to Others instead of recovering. What do the allies they tend get?
choices: They add the tender's Medicine modifier to their recovery die roll
They gain an advantage on their recovery die
One injury is shortened by 1 day
explanation: Tend to Others has you forgo your own recovery; the willing allies resting with you add your Medicine modifier to their recovery die rolls.
verify: they add your Medicine modifier to their recovery die roll

question: In combat, an effect lasts '1 round'. When does it end?
choices: At the end of the current round
At the end of the affected character's next turn
At the beginning of the same turn phase (fast PC, fast NPC, etc.) on the next round
explanation: Note which phase the effect began in — fast PC, fast NPC, slow PC or slow NPC. It lasts until the start of that same phase on the next round.
verify: The effect lasts until the beginning of that phase on the next round

question: How long can a character go without food before suffering ill effects?
choices: A number of days equal to their Willpower
A number of days equal to their Strength
explanation: You can go days equal to your Willpower without food; each further day makes you Exhausted [−1]. Reaching Exhausted [−10] or worse is fatal. Water is harsher: Exhausted [−1] from the first day without it.
verify: up to your Willpower score before you begin to feel ill effects

question: During a scene with an event track in play, how do the event's slots get filled?
choices: The GM fills one slot each round
Players and GM spend Opportunities or Complications to fill slots instead of using them normally
Each failed test fills a slot automatically
Slots fill when a character takes an injury
explanation: Opportunities can be spent to fill positive event slots and Complications (spent by the GM) to fill negative ones, giving up their usual effects. The event triggers when the last slot fills.
verify: spending Opportunities and Complications to fill slots

question: Using the downtime Training activity, how long does it typically take to learn a new expertise, and at what cost?
choices: 20 days or longer at 5 marks per day
explanation: Training for a new expertise (even a specialist one) usually takes 20+ days at 5 marks per day, and normally needs a relevant skill test. Research, by comparison, is about 10+ days at 3 marks per day.
verify: It usually takes 20 days or longer to learn a new expertise

question: What does the Self-Reflection downtime activity allow?
choices: Swearing an Ideal without a goal
Rebuilding your character (e.g. swapping talents or skill ranks) at the same level, after 10+ days at 5 marks per day
explanation: Ten or more days of self-reflection (5 marks/day) let you rebuild your character at your current level with GM approval. Prerequisites still apply, and rewards don't count toward earlier-level prerequisites.
verify: If you dedicate 10 or more days to self-reflection

question: A PC in armor with deflect 2 is reduced to 0 health. They already have one injury. They roll a 9 on the injury roll. What happens?
choices: Flesh wound — heals after a long rest
explanation: 9 + 2 (deflect) − 5 (one existing injury) = 6, which is in the 6–15 shallow injury band (1d6 days). They're also Unconscious.
verify: Add the deflect value of any armor you’re wearing

question: An unarmored PC with two existing injuries suffers another and rolls a 7 on the injury roll. What's the outcome?
explanation: 7 − 10 (two existing injuries × 5) = −3, which falls in the −5 to 0 band: a permanent injury.
verify: −5 to 0 Permanent Injury

question: A PC lies Unconscious at 0 health. An enemy spends an attack on them and hits for 4 damage. What happens?
choices: They suffer another injury and make another injury roll
They wake up from the pain
explanation: Each time you take damage while at 0 health, you suffer another injury, with the −5 per existing injury making it more dangerous. (Enemies typically ignore Unconscious characters unless they have a strong reason.)
verify: Each time you take damage while at 0 health, you suffer another injury

question: A PC is Exhausted [−2] from travel, then a poison makes them Exhausted [−1]. They roll a Survival test totaling 16. What is the final result?
explanation: Exhausted is cumulative: −2 and −1 make a −3 penalty, applied after calculating the result. 16 − 3 = 13.
verify: so you now subtract 3 from the result of all tests

question: A PC with Speed 3 (30 ft movement) becomes Enhanced [+2 Speed]. What changes?
choices: Movement rises to 40 ft and Speed-based skill tests get +2; Physical defense stays the same
Everything Speed affects, including Physical defense, rises by 2
explanation: Enhanced Speed 5 uses the 40 ft movement band and adds +2 to Agility, Light Weaponry, Stealth and Thievery tests — but Enhanced never changes defenses.
verify: Increase your movement rate from 30 feet to 40 feet

question: A PC with 30 ft of movement has moved 15 ft when a trap makes them Slowed. How much farther can they move with this Move?
explanation: If you become Slowed mid-movement, halve your remaining movement, rounded up — an exception to the usual round-down rule. Half of 15 is 7.5, rounded up to 8.
verify: halve your remaining movement (rounded up)

question: During the fast PC phase, a PC's ability makes an enemy Disoriented for 1 round. When does it wear off?
choices: At the end of the enemy's next turn
At the start of the fast PC phase on the next round
At the end of this round
At the start of the slow NPC phase this round
explanation: Round-based durations last until the start of the same phase in which they began, on the next round. It began in the fast PC phase, so it ends when the next fast PC phase starts.
verify: the fast PC phase, the fast NPC phase, the slow PC phase, or the slow NPC phase

question: You've put a positive event, 'Reinforcements Arrive', on the table with Opportunity slots. An enemy NPC rolls a Complication. What can that Complication do?
choices: Nothing — NPCs can't interact with events
It can fill a slot on the PCs' positive event
It must fill a negative event slot
It cancels a filled Opportunity slot
explanation: NPC contributions are inverted: an enemy's Opportunities feed events that are bad for the PCs, and its Complications feed events that are good for them.
verify: their Complications fill slots toward events with positive implications

question: A PC with Willpower 2 is lost in the wilds with plenty of water but no food for 5 days. What's their condition?
explanation: They can go 2 days (their Willpower) without food. Each day after that adds Exhausted [−1]: days 3, 4 and 5 make Exhausted [−3].
verify: For each day beyond this that you go without sufficient food

question: After an hour's break between fights, a PC at low health and low focus rolls a 6 on their recovery die. What can they do with it?
choices: Recover 6 health only — focus needs a long rest
Split the 6 between health and focus however they like (e.g. 4 and 2)
explanation: After a short rest you add the recovery die result to health, focus or any combination of the two.
verify: you might choose to recover 3 health and 2 focus
